summary: All notebook semantic and integration checks passed. The notebook demonstrates only BADGE, preserves predicted-label gradient embeddings and seeded k-MEANS++ on the live acquisition path, and retrains a fresh model after every acquisition.

checks_summary.note: The loop evaluates held-out test labels; final accuracy is an execution-time smoke-gate outcome rather than a narrative substitution.
Sections 4 and 5 accurately describe the gradient-embedding, k-MEANS++, pool-index mapping, and fresh-retraining paths exercised below them.
The cited Algorithm 1, Section 3, Eq. 1, Appendix A Algorithm 2, and Section 4 locations match the referenced paper mechanisms.
The loop computes held-out test accuracy for the initially trained model and for each newly retrained round model before appending each curve point.
A new model is built before initial training and inside every acquisition-round iteration, consistent with the paper's no-warm-start protocol.
Pool-relative positions are mapped through unlabeled_idx, then unioned into labeled_idx and removed by set difference without positional offsets.
The initial evaluation is recorded once and range(cfg["num_rounds"]) performs one acquisition, retraining, and evaluation per round, yielding num_rounds + 1 points.
The notebook describes sampling proportional to squared nearest-center distance and does not make a contradictory rank-direction claim.
The live notebook path calls BADGE selection on predicted-label gradient embeddings with seeded k-MEANS++ and preserves the required fresh-retraining control without forbidden substitutions.

caveats: The notebook is intentionally unexecuted at this production stage; the smoke gate must confirm the observed final held-out accuracy exceeds chance.
